sources.entry: Aster - Native macOS terminal workspace built with AppKit and Ghostty, with recursive splits, file browsing, and previews.

summary.one_liner: Aster is a native macOS terminal workspace built with AppKit and the Ghostty terminal engine, combining recursive terminal splits with a file browser, editor, and previewer.
summary.what_it_does: Aster lets you arrange Ghostty-powered terminals alongside file browsers, editors, and previews using recursive horizontal and vertical splits, with multiple tabs. It has a File Pane that previews source code, Markdown/RST, images, PDF, diffs, hex, and Agent transcripts. It tracks Claude Code and Codex session titles, running status, and completion notifications. Workspace layouts can be saved as .asterrecipe files and restored on launch, and it supports native SSH tabs and remote machine workspaces via a server-side session service. Shell integration covers zsh, Bash, and fish, with local autocomplete backed by Fig command specs. Built-in Sparkle 2 handles software updates.
use_cases: Run terminals side by side with file previews on macOS
Save and restore a workspace layout
Monitor Claude Code or Codex sessions in a terminal
Open SSH sessions and remote workspaces in tabs
Preview Markdown, PDFs, and images next to a shell
Customize terminal themes and keyboard shortcuts
notable: Native AppKit UI with no SwiftUI/Hosting bridge layer
Recursive splits that mix terminals, file browsers, editors, and previews
Local autocomplete using 714 Fig command specs
Workspace import/export as .asterrecipe files with session restore
Automatic updates via Sparkle 2 with EdDSA signature and notarization checks
caveats: Released DMG requires macOS 14 or later and an Apple silicon Mac
Building from source needs Swift 6.2, Zig 0.15.2, and the Xcode Metal Toolchain
Ad-hoc builds have automatic updates disabled
